strengths: Substantial and well-curated dataset (TSR-SUITE) with 23.6K samples across 10 diverse domains, with rigorous hierarchical annotation pipeline ensuring quality
Clear problem formulation addressing real limitations of existing time series QA datasets with well-motivated design principles
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ID/OOD testing, ablations, multiple tasks, and cross-task transfer analysis
Practical and timely contribution addressing genuine gap in LLM temporal reasoning capabilities
Well-supported empirical findings with clear demonstration of how temporal priors and joint training enable better time series reasoning
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: applies existing techniques (SFT + GRPO RL) without novel architectures, loss functions, or learning algorithms

Significant and unexplained OOD performance drops (4-10% on multiple tasks) contradict claims of 'strong out-of-distribution generalization'; OOD evaluation limited to geographic splits within same domains
Unfair model comparisons: TimeOmni-1 trained on TSR-SUITE while baselines (GPT-4.1) are not; lacks controlled comparison with baselines fine-tuned on identical data
Task 3 evaluation methodology concerns: Event-aware Forecasting allows predictions misaligned with ground truth if 'plausible and well-justified,' introducing subjective assessment ambiguity
Insufficient mechanistic analysis: paper shows temporal priors and joint training help but lacks deep explanation of why; no investigation of learned representations or failure modes
Generalization limited to same 10 domains (only geographic shifts): lacks evaluation on fundamentally novel domain types; all tasks remain discrete/sequence-output selection
Missing comparison to classical time series baselines (ARIMA, Prophet, domain-specific models) and limited ablation studies on design choices
Reproducibility issues: no code/data availability plan mentioned; implementation details sparse; temporal prior injection method not fully specified
No ethical discussion of real-world deployment risks when model produces incorrect temporal predictions used for actual decision-making

strengths: Comprehensive and well-designed dataset (TSR-Suite) with 23K+ carefully annotated samples across 10 domains addressing identified gaps in time series reasoning benchmarks
Strong empirical results showing consistent top-2 performance across all four reasoning tasks with significant improvements over baselines (40.6% on causality discovery ID, 28.1% OOD vs GPT-4.1)
Thorough experimental evaluation including multiple baselines, ID/OOD analysis, detailed ablation studies, and progressive capability transfer analysis
Clear problem identification with well-articulated motivations grounded in concrete limitations of existing datasets (surface-level understanding, insufficient context, lack of reasoning tasks)
Thoughtful two-stage training approach with human-guided reasoning priors (Stage 1) and task-grounded reward refinement (Stage 2) that addresses identified technical gaps
Demonstrates joint training across diverse reasoning capabilities yields mutual benefits, supporting practical unified model paradigm for time series reasoning
Excellent presentation with clear task definitions, informative visualizations, detailed case studies, and comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility
Addresses real gap in LLM capabilities for complex time series reasoning, with potential for significant impact on future research in this area
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty - primarily applies standard SFT + RL techniques to a new dataset rather than introducing novel architectures or methods specifically designed for temporal reasoning
Dataset quality validation concerns including missing inter-annotator agreement statistics, limited analysis of annotation disagreements, and no thorough analysis of TSR-Suite's own potential biases
Incomplete baseline comparisons lacking recent LLM variants (GPT-4 Turbo, Claude 3, Llama 3) and other LLM-based time series approaches; most baselines are specialized models
Task 3 (event-aware forecasting) has inherent formulation limitations allowing spurious solutions and potentially biasing learned behaviors; reward design appears ad-hoc with limited justification
Limited generalization analysis - OOD evaluation restricted to geographic shifts within existing domains without testing on truly novel time series types or task formulations
Missing failure case analysis - limited discussion of where TimeOmni-1 struggles or which reasoning patterns are challenging; no systematic error analysis provided
Computational efficiency not addressed - no analysis of inference latency, practical deployment constraints with 8 H100 GPUs required, or comparison with smaller faster models
Incomplete evaluation metrics - forecasting uses only MAE without alternative metrics (MAPE, RMSE, directional accuracy); valid response rates remain low indicating substantial failure modes
Reproducibility limitations including unclear dataset release plan, difficult-to-replicate hierarchical annotation process, and high computational barriers
Insufficient theoretical justification for why hierarchical reasoning priors should improve time series understanding or how time series reasoning differs from other reasoning domains

strengths: Addresses a relevant gap: scarcity of high-quality, reasoning-critical time series data with well-defined tasks

Substantial dataset contribution: TSR-Suite contains 23K+ carefully curated and annotated samples across 4 complementary reasoning tasks with clear design principles (perception, extrapolation, decision-making)
Comprehensive evaluation methodology: includes in-distribution and out-of-distribution testbeds, multiple metrics, ablation studies, scaling analysis, and external benchmark validation
Rigorous two-stage training approach: principled methodology combining supervised fine-tuning with human-guided temporal priors and reinforcement learning with task-grounded rewards
Thorough experimental analysis: includes prompt robustness tests, joint training benefits analysis, and reward sensitivity analysis
Strong reproducibility commitment: detailed hyperparameters, prompts, promised code/data release, and clear annotation process documentation
Clear problem formulation: well-articulated limitations of existing time series datasets and principled design principles for reasoning-critical tasks
weaknesses: Critical contradiction in results: External benchmarks (MTBench, TimeSeriesExam) show degraded performance compared to base models, directly contradicting claims of top-2 performance and improved time series reasoning capabilities
Limited technical novelty: Standard LLM fine-tuning approach; two-stage training (SFT+RL) is conventional practice with no novel architectural innovations
Weak task-specific performance: Task 3 (Event-aware Forecasting) achieves only ~26% Success Rate, and OOD performance drops substantially on multiple tasks, questioning generalization claims

Dataset annotation bias: Using GPT-4.1 for annotation creates circular dependency when comparing against GPT-4.1; Task 3 lacks proper ground truth (acknowledged open-ended forecasting with noisy labels)
Evaluation methodology concerns: Success Rate metric overly stringent for forecasting; selective result reporting; limited baseline comparisons missing recent strong models (GPT-4o, Claude)

Questionable design justification: Why inject temporal priors via SFT vs. architecture? Text-based vs. embedding-based approaches show minimal difference (Table 8). Task 3 formulation conflates forecasting with reasoning
Weak generalization evidence: Figures 13-14 show scaling plateaus and non-monotonic behavior; joint training benefits (Finding 4) not fully validated; OOD evaluation uses only temporal/spatial shifts

Missing critical analysis: No ablation on task formulations, insufficient distinction between pattern matching vs. genuine reasoning, no failure case analysis, insufficient justification for task choice
Scaling behavior concerns: Non-monotonic scaling patterns for Task 3 not adequately discussed; some tasks show worse OOD than ID performance by significant margins

strengths: Substantial dataset contribution: TSR-Suite with 23K+ carefully curated time series reasoning samples across four well-designed tasks (perception, extrapolation, decision-making, causality discovery), with 2.3K human-annotated chain-of-thought samples

Exceptional evaluation rigor: Comprehensive assessment including ID/OOD testbeds, external benchmarks (MTBench, TimeSeriesExam, CaTS-Bench), extensive ablations on training stages/strategies, scaling analysis, and general reasoning benchmarks demonstrating maintained capability
Strong and consistent empirical results: Achieves Top-2 performance across all tasks, outperforms GPT-4.1 by 40.6% (ID) and 28.1% (OOD) on causality discovery, maintains ~93% valid response rate

Methodologically sound approach: Two-stage training justified by clear empirical findings; two design principles (QA-pairs reward reasoning, context sufficiency) guide task formulation; findings about temporal priors and joint training are actionable
Excellent reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters, system prompts, structured templates for annotation, training dynamics visualizations, reward sensitivity analysis, and promised code release
Well-articulated problem motivation: Clearly identifies genuine limitations in existing time series models regarding data scarcity, undefined tasks, and insufficient complex reasoning capabilities
Clear presentation: Well-structured writing with effective visualizations clearly communicating methodology, findings, and comprehensive experimental results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Primary contribution is engineering/combination of standard techniques (SFT + RL, GRPO algorithm, text tokenization of time series) rather than methodological innovation

Dataset quality concerns: Only 9.8% of 23K samples (2.3K) manually annotated with detailed reasoning chains; ~20K samples rely on automated generation via LLM Analyzer, limiting 'gold standard' claims. No inter-rater agreement metrics reported

Insufficient validation of temporal reasoning specificity: Evaluation includes general reasoning benchmarks but doesn't deeply probe what specific temporal reasoning patterns are learned or distinguish genuine temporal reasoning from sophisticated pattern matching

Context sufficiency principle inadequately validated: Principle 2 is important but vague; limited validation that auxiliary context C is truly sufficient across all tasks, particularly for causality discovery with inherent ambiguities

Task design inconsistencies: Task 3 (Event-aware Forecasting) is prediction-focused rather than reasoning-focused, differing significantly from other tasks; Task 4 might be better framed as 'cost optimization under constraints.' These differences undermine 'unified reasoning model' framing

Text tokenization trade-offs underexplored: While practical, tokenizing time series introduces quantization errors; brief acknowledgment in Section F.3 but insufficient impact analysis. Alternative embedding-based approaches not explored
Limited failure analysis: No systematic error analysis, identification of failure modes, or exploration of which time series types/reasoning steps the model struggles with
Generalization limitations: OOD testing limited to selected domains within same distribution family; no evaluation on truly novel domains absent from TSR-Suite
Incomplete technical details: Computational costs not clearly reported; full human annotation process details missing; inference efficiency not compared with baselines
